x0​=11​,a0​=3.

(2)

x2​=x1​−31​=11​+3,a2​=6.

11​=[3;3,6​].​

zn​=pn​+qn​11​.

z1​=10+311​=23+11​​(3+11​)=23+11​​z0​.

zn+1​=an+1​zn​+zn−1​,

The function h is continuous, with

Now suppose 0,1∈f([0,1]). For any y∈[0,1], choose a,b∈[0,1] with f(a)=0 and f(b)=1. Applying the intermediate value theorem to f on the interval with endpoints a,b gives a point x with f(x)=y. Thus f is a surjective function.

g=h−1∘f∘h:A→A

h−1(f(h(a)))=a,

iv

Words: 64 Articles: 1
2F OurBigBook.com

Solution

Words: 64
iv OurBigBook.com
The closed unit disc has the fixed-point property by the Brouwer fixed-point theorem. The annulus admits the fixed-point-free rotation of an annulus, for example
R(x,y)=(−x,−y),
(17)
which is continuous, maps the annulus to itself, and has no fixed point because the origin is not in the annulus. If the disc and annulus were homeomorphic, the homeomorphism invariance of the fixed-point property would give the annulus the fixed-point property, a contradiction. Therefore they are not homeomorphic.
Solved by gpt-5.6-sol high.

v

Words: 77 Articles: 1

Solution

Words: 77
v OurBigBook.com
No. Take
B=[0,1]×{0}⊂R2.
(18)
It contains more than one point and has the fixed-point property of a closed interval, but it is not homeomorphic to the closed unit disc. Indeed, deleting any point (t,0) with 0<t<1 disconnects B, so such a point is a cut point. Deleting one point from a two-dimensional closed disc leaves a path-connected space. Since being a cut point is preserved by homeomorphisms, the two spaces cannot be homeomorphic. This gives the required counterexample.

a OurBigBook.com
For the standard dot product on F2n​, the dual code is
C⊥={y∈F2n​:y⋅c=0 for every c∈C}.​
(19)
It is an intersection of kernels of linear functions, and is therefore a linear code.
Let σ denote cyclic right shift. If y∈C⊥ and c∈C, then
(σy)⋅c=y⋅(σ−1c).
(20)
A cyclic code is closed under both σ and σ−1, so σ−1c∈C and the right-hand side vanishes. Hence σy∈C⊥, proving directly that the dual of a cyclic code is cyclic.
Identify words with polynomials in F2​[X]/(Xn−1). If the generator polynomial of a cyclic code is the monic divisor g(X) and
g(X)h(X)=Xn−1,
(21)
then the generator polynomial of C⊥ is the monic reciprocal
g⊥(X)=h∗(X)=Xdeghh(X−1)/h(0).​
(22)
Equivalently, the parity-check polynomial of one code becomes, after reversal, the generator polynomial of its dual.

b OurBigBook.com
Over F2​, subtraction equals addition. The polynomial X7−1 has the factorization
X7−1=(X+1)(X3+X+1)(X3+X2+1).​
(23)
The two cubic factors have no root in F2​, so they are irreducible, and they are reciprocal to one another. Put
f=X3+X+1,f∗=X3+X2+1.
(24)
Every cyclic code corresponds to one monic divisor of X7−1. The complete list is
g(X)1X+1ff∗(X+1)f(X+1)f∗ff∗=1+X+⋯+X6(X+1)ff∗=X7−1​parameters[7,7,1][7,6,2][7,4,3][7,4,3][7,3,4][7,3,4][7,1,7][7,0]​codewhole-space linear codeeven-weight binary codeHamming codereversed Hamming codebinary simplex codereversed binary simplex codebinary repetition codezero code.​​
(25)
Thus the two cubic generators give the two cyclic coordinate orientations of Hamming's [7,4,3] code. Their duals have generators (X+1)f and (X+1)f∗ and are the [7,3,4] simplex codes. The remaining four are the familiar whole-space, even-weight, repetition, and zero codes. This is the complete classification of binary cyclic codes of length seven.

A grammar G=(Σ,V,P,S) is a right-linear regular grammar when every production has one of the forms
A→wBorA→w,​
(26)
where A,B∈V and w∈Σ∗. Thus a production has at most one variable on its right-hand side, and that variable is at the right end.

ii

Words: 108 Articles: 1
4I OurBigBook.com

Solution

Words: 108
ii OurBigBook.com
We prove the claim by induction on the length of the grammar derivation from S. At length zero the sentential form is S=ϵS, which has the required form.
Suppose the current sentential form is wA. Because w is terminal, the only symbol to which a production can apply is A. A production A→uB produces
wA⇒wuB,
(27)
again a terminal word followed by one variable. A production A→u produces the terminal word wu. Once a completely terminal word is reached, no further production can apply. The induction proves the sentential form of a right-linear regular grammar: every reachable α is either wA or w.
Solved by gpt-5.6-sol high.

iii OurBigBook.com
In every derivation beginning at wA, the terminal prefix w remains unchanged because no production has a terminal on its left-hand side. By the sentential-form result, each step rewrites the sole variable at the right and appends terminals immediately before its successor variable. Hence
wA⇒∗vB
(28)
forces v=wu for some u∈Σ∗. Removing the inert prefix w from every sentential form in the derivation gives
A⇒∗uB.​
(29)

4I OurBigBook.com

Solution

Words: 128
iv OurBigBook.com
An accepting derivation in a right-linear grammar has the form
S⇒w1​A1​⇒w1​w2​A2​⇒⋯⇒w1​⋯wm​,
(30)
with one active variable until the final terminal production.
If no variable repeated on any accepting derivation, an accepting derivation could contain at most ∣V∣ variable occurrences. Since the production set is finite, only finitely many such derivations and hence finitely many terminal words would exist. The hypothesis that L(G) is infinite therefore supplies an accepting derivation in which some variable A occurs twice.
Split this derivation at the two occurrences:
S⇒∗uA,A⇒∗vA,A⇒∗z,
(31)
where u,v,z∈Σ∗. The first segment makes A an accessible variable of a regular grammar, the middle segment makes it a looping variable of a regular grammar, and the last makes it a terminable variable of a regular grammar. Thus A has all three properties, proving the accessible looping terminable variable criterion.

iii

Words: 177 Articles: 1
5J OurBigBook.com

Solution

Words: 177
iii OurBigBook.com
Treat make as a categorical predictor, converting it to a factor explicitly if necessary:
fit3 <- lm(log(price) ~ mpg + psngr + length + width + weight + factor(make), data = cars)
The models are nested. The first nested-model F-test compares fit2 with the intercept-only fit1. Adding the five quantitative predictors reduces the residual sum of squares from 8584.0 to 3349.1, with
F=69.7334,p<2.2×10−16.
(32)
There is overwhelming evidence that these quantitative car properties jointly improve the model.
The second test compares fit3 with fit2. Adding make reduces the residual sum of squares further to 840.8, with
F=5.3891,p=2.541×10−8.
(33)
Thus manufacturer has a highly significant effect even after adjusting for the five quantitative properties, and fit3 is preferred among these nested models.
There are 93 observations because the intercept-only model has 92=93−1 residual degrees of freedom. The make term uses 31 additional degrees of freedom. By the degrees of freedom of a factor predictor, a factor with m represented levels contributes m−1 degrees of freedom when an intercept is present. Hence
m−1=31,m=32​
(34)
unique manufacturers occur in the dataset.

7E (Further Complex Methods)

Words: 291 Articles: 1
Paper 4 OurBigBook.com

Solution

Words: 291
7E OurBigBook.com
The Papperitz symbol
P⎩⎨⎧​001−c​10c−a−b​∞ab​z​​⎭⎬⎫​
(41)
specifies a second-order Fuchsian differential equation. The first row lists its three distinct regular singular points 0,1,∞; z is the independent variable. The two entries below each singular point are its characteristic exponents. Thus local solutions have leading behaviors
1, z1−c(z→0),
(42)
1, (1−z)c−a−b(z→1),
(43)
and, with the usual convention at infinity,
z−a, z−b(z→∞).
(44)
When an exponent difference is an integer, a logarithmic second solution may replace the naive second Frobenius power. The entries obey the Fuchs relation
0+(1−c)+0+(c−a−b)+a+b=1.
(45)
For a second-order equation with exactly three regular singular points, these exponent data determine the equation up to multiplication by a nonzero function; there is no accessory parameter. The symbol is therefore the one for the Gauss hypergeometric equation. Its distinguished solution F(a,b;c;z) is the exponent-zero solution analytic at zero and normalized to one there. For the ordinary power-series definition one assumes c∈/{0,−1,−2,…}, with exceptional parameter values handled separately or by continuation.
Now put
u=z−1z​,Y(z)=F(a,c−b;c;u).
(46)
The hypergeometric equation in u has exponent pairs
(0,1−c) at u=0,(0,b−a) at u=1,(a,c−b) at u=∞.
(47)
The Möbius transformation of a Papperitz symbol sends
u=0,1,∞⟵z=0,∞,1,
(48)
so Y has symbol
P⎩⎨⎧​001−c​1ac−b​∞0b−a​z​​⎭⎬⎫​.
(49)
On the other hand, F(a,b;c;z) has exponent pairs
(0,1−c),(0,c−a−b),(a,b)
(50)
at 0,1,∞. Multiplication by (1−z)a applies the dependent-variable rescaling of a Papperitz symbol: it adds a to both exponents at z=1 and subtracts a from both at infinity. Hence
(1−z)aF(a,b;c;z)
(51)
has exactly the same three exponent pairs as Y.
Both functions are analytic near z=0 and equal one at z=0, so uniqueness of the normalized exponent-zero hypergeometric solution gives the Pfaff transformation
F(a,c−b;c;z−1z​)=(1−z)aF(a,b;c;z).​
(52)
The identity first holds near zero with the branch of (1−z)a equal to one there, and then extends by analytic continuation on any domain where compatible branches are chosen.

8D OurBigBook.com
An adiabatic invariant remains constant to leading order when a system parameter changes on a timescale much longer than one period. For a periodic one-degree-of-freedom system, the adiabatic invariance of the action supplies such an invariant.
The momentum magnitude between collisions is p0​=2mE​. A complete orbit crosses the gap once in each direction, so the unnormalized action used in the question is
I=∮pdq=2Lp0​=2L2mE​.​
(53)
Consequently
dEdI​=2mE​2Lm​=2E/m​2L​=T,
(54)
because the speed is 2E/m​ and the round-trip distance is 2L.
When L(t) varies adiabatically, conservation of the adiabatic particle between moving parallel walls action gives
E(t)=E(0)(L(t)L(0)​)2.​
(55)
A moving wall does work at each collision: an approaching wall raises the particle's energy and a receding wall lowers it. Elasticity holds in the instantaneous rest frame of the wall.

The Flatness problem is that the observed cosmological density parameter is close to Ω=1, although in an ordinary decelerating universe any departure from one grows with time. Extrapolation backward therefore requires implausibly precise early cancellation of the curvature term.
The cosmological perfect-fluid continuity equation is
ρ˙​+3H(ρ+P)=0.
(56)
Consequently
dtd​(ρa2)=a2ρ˙​+2aa˙ρ=−Ha2(ρ+3P).
(57)
For an expanding universe H>0. If
ρ+3P<0,
(58)
then ρa2 increases. The Friedmann equation implies
​Ω−1−1​=ρa2constant×∣k∣​.
(59)
It therefore decreases during this period, driving Ω toward one. By the Friedmann acceleration equation, the same condition gives a¨>0 when the cosmological constant is included in the effective fluid. This is the inflationary solution of the flatness problem.
For the scalar field, the slow-roll approximation means
ϕ˙​2≪V(ϕ),∣ϕ¨​∣≪3H∣ϕ˙​∣.

The Chebyshev alternation theorem says that a polynomial P of degree at most n is a best uniform approximation to f∈C([0,1]) if and only if there are n+2 points
0≤t0​<t1​<⋯<tn+1​≤1
(102)
and a sign ε∈{1,−1} for which
f(tj​)−P(tj​)=ε(−1)j∥f−P∥∞​.
(103)
This is the equiripple criterion.
To prove sufficiency, put E=∥f−P∥∞​ and suppose that another polynomial Q of degree at most n satisfies ∥f−Q∥∞​<E. At every tj​, the difference R=Q−P must have the same sign as f−P; hence its signs alternate at the n+2 ordered points. The intermediate value theorem then gives at least one distinct root of R in every interval (tj​,tj+1​), for at least n+1 roots in all. The Lagrange root bound over a field forces the nonzero polynomial R to have degree at least n+1, contradicting degR≤n. Therefore no Q gives a smaller error, and P is best.

a OurBigBook.com
Assume the axiom of choice. By the well-ordering theorem, every set is bijective with an ordinal, and hence with an initial ordinal. Any two ordinals are comparable, so for any sets K,L either K injects into L or L injects into K. Transitivity is immediate, and antisymmetry on cardinalities follows from the Cantor-Schröder-Bernstein theorem. Thus cardinal comparison is a total order.
Conversely, assume the cardinal comparability principle. Given any set X, let h(X) be its Hartogs ordinal. By Hartogs theorem, there is no injection h(X)→X. Comparability therefore supplies an injection X→h(X). Pulling the ordinal order back to X gives a well-order of X. Hence every set can be well-ordered, and the well-ordering theorem implies the axiom of choice.

Translation invariance makes this form S1-invariant, and positivity is preserved, proving unitarity. Since S1 is abelian, the operators ρ(z) commute; since they are unitary, they are normal. g(x,y,z)=​100​x10​zy1​​.

k(X)≅k(Y).

dimX=trdegk​k(X).

Now let K/C be a finitely generated field extension. Choose field generators a1​,…,am​ and set
A=C[a1​,…,am​]⊆K.

Then A is a finitely generated integral C-algebra and Frac(A)=K. The affine irreducible variety
X0​=SpecA

has function field K. Embed X0​ as a closed affine subvariety of some affine space AN, identify that affine space with the standard open chart of projective space PN, and take the projective closure X of X0​. The closure of an irreducible topological space is irreducible, and X0​ is dense and open in X. Thus X is a projective variety and
k(X)=k(X0​)=K.
(256)
This constructs the projective model of a finitely generated field.
For the curve
X=V(y2−x(x−1)2),

t=x−1y​.

t2=x,y=t(x−1)=t(t2−1).

A smooth projective curve in the projective plane of degree d has, by the genus of a smooth plane curve formula,
g=2(d−1)(d−2)​.

Its genus can be zero only for d=1 or d=2. Conversely, a projective line and every smooth conic over C are rational, so each is birational to X. Therefore the required degrees are exactly
d=1 or d=2​.

35A OurBigBook.com

Solution

Words: 170
a OurBigBook.com
The Clausius statement of the second law says that no cyclic device can have as its sole effect the transfer of heat from a colder reservoir to a hotter one. The Kelvin-Planck statement of the second law says that no cyclic device can have as its sole effect the extraction of heat from one reservoir and its complete conversion into work.
Suppose first that the Clausius statement fails. Use the forbidden device to return to a hot reservoir the heat QC​ rejected by an ordinary heat engine. The combined device extracts QH​−QC​ from the hot reservoir and converts all of it into work, violating the Kelvin--Planck statement.
Conversely, suppose the Kelvin--Planck statement fails. Use the work produced by the forbidden one-reservoir engine to drive an ordinary refrigerator. The engine's heat withdrawal and the refrigerator's heat discharge cancel by the work-energy balance, leaving only a transfer of heat from the cold reservoir to the hot reservoir with no external work. This violates the Clausius statement. Each statement therefore implies the other, so the two forms of the Second law of thermodynamics are equivalent.

∇ϕ+​⟶Uex​(y→+∞),∇ϕ−​⟶Uex​(y→−∞).
(420)
Every shear layer is a material interface. The exact kinematic boundary condition at y=h+η is
ϕ+,y​=ηt​+ϕ+,x​ηx​,ϕ0,y​=ηt​+ϕ0,x​ηx​,
(421)
and at y=−h−η it is
ϕ−,y​=−ηt​−ϕ−,x​ηx​,ϕ0,y​=−ηt​−ϕ0,x​ηx​.
(422)
Here each equation is evaluated on the indicated moving interface.
Finally, pressure continuity is the dynamic boundary condition for an inviscid interface. The Unsteady Bernoulli equation gives
ϕ+,t​+21​∣∇ϕ+​∣2=ϕ0,t​+21​∣∇ϕ0​∣2(y=h+η),
(423)
ϕ−,t​+21​∣∇ϕ−​∣2=ϕ0,t​+21​∣∇ϕ0​∣2(y=−h−η),
(424)
after absorbing spatially constant functions of time into the potentials.

The displacement must have small relative amplitude and small slope,
h∣η∣​≪1,∣ηx​∣≪1.
(425)
Write the potentials as perturbations of the base flow,
ϕ±​=Ux+φ±​,ϕ0​=φ0​,
(426)
with ∣∇φ±​∣/U and ∣∇φ0​∣/U small. A linearization evaluates the conditions at the unperturbed lines y=±h and discards products of perturbations. At y=h this gives
φ+,y​=ηt​+Uηx​,φ0,y​=ηt​,φ+,t​+Uφ+,x​=φ0,t​,
(427)
whereas at y=−h it gives
φ−,y​=−ηt​−Uηx​,φ0,y​=−ηt​,φ−,t​+Uφ−,x​=φ0,t​.
(428)
The perturbation potentials remain harmonic functions, and their gradients decay at the corresponding far fields.

d OurBigBook.com
The linearized equations are homogeneous and have constant coefficients in x and t. Consequently, spatial Fourier modes evolve independently, and the superposition principle reconstructs arbitrary sufficiently regular initial disturbances from them. It is therefore enough to seek the normal modes
η(x,t)=Re{η0​eikx+σt}.
(429)
Here the real k is the wavenumber, σ is the possibly complex temporal exponent, and taking the real part produces a physical displacement.

e OurBigBook.com
Put q=∣k∣. Decay at infinity and the symmetry of the disturbance suggest the mode potentials
φ+​=Ae−q(y−h)eikx+σt,φ−​=Aeq(y+h)eikx+σt,
(430)
φ0​=Bcosh(qy)eikx+σt.
(431)
The middle potential is an even function of y because its vertical derivative must take opposite values at the two interfaces. The upper kinematic conditions give
−qA=(σ+ikU)η0​,qBsinh(qh)=ση0​.
(432)
The lower conditions give the same two relations. The upper dynamic condition is
(σ+ikU)A=σBcosh(qh).
(433)
Eliminating A, B and η0​ yields the dispersion relation
(σ+ikU)2+σ2coth(qh)=0​.
(434)
Writing C=coth(qh), its two roots are
σ=1+C−ikU±qUC​​​.
(435)
For every real k=0, C>0 and one root has the positive growth rate
Reσ=1+coth(∣k∣h)∣k∣Ucoth(∣k∣h)​​>0.
(436)
Thus every nonzero wavenumber is linearly unstable in this inviscid vortex sheet model; k=0 is neutral.

Solution

Words: 73
f OurBigBook.com
When ∣k∣h≫1, the two shear layers are separated by many disturbance decay lengths. Since coth(∣k∣h)→1, the roots reduce to
σ∼−2ikU​±2∣k∣U​​.
(437)
This is exactly the Kelvin-Helmholtz instability of one isolated vortex sheet separating equal-density streams of speeds U and 0: the pattern travels at their mean speed U/2, while its unstable amplitude grows at rate ∣k∣U/2. The exponentially weak interaction between the two layers disappears in this short-wavelength limit.

The one-dimensional mass flux and momentum flux are respectively
Jm​=ρu,Jp​=p+ρu2.
(438)
In a steady flow, the conservation laws make both the mass flux and the given energy flux
JE​=u(p+W+21​ρu2)
(439)
constant. Wherever Jm​=0, their ratio is therefore constant:
Jm​JE​​=ρp+W​+21​u2=γ−1γ​ρp​+21​u2=C,
(440)
where W=p/(γ−1) is the internal energy per unit volume of the ideal gas. This is the required steady-flow energy integral.

b OurBigBook.com
Work in the shock frame, and let the positive upstream and downstream speeds be w0​ and w1​. The Rankine-Hugoniot conditions for a perfect gas give conservation of mass and momentum:
ρ0​w0​=ρ1​w1​,p0​+ρ0​w02​=p1​+ρ1​w12​.
(441)
Put
r=ρ0​ρ1​​,p0​p1​​=1+β.
(442)
Mass conservation gives w1​=w0​/r, and momentum conservation then gives
w02​=ρ0​p0​​r−1βr​.(1)
(443)
Applying the energy integral from part (a) on the two sides gives
γ−1γ​ρ0​p0​​+21​w02​=γ−1γ​ρ0​rp0​(1+β)​+21​r2w02​​.(2)
(444)
Substitution of (1) into (2), followed by cancellation of p0​/ρ0​, yields
2β(r+1)​=γ−1γ​(1+β−r).
(445)
Solving this linear equation for the density ratio gives
ρ0​ρ1​​=r=2γ+(γ−1)β2γ+(γ+1)β​​.
(446)

Solution

c OurBigBook.com
The Taylor series of the shock density ratio at β=0 is
ρ0​ρ1​​=1+γβ​−2γ2γ−1​β2+O(β3).(1)
(447)
For a reversible adiabatic process, p/p0​=(ρ/ρ0​)γ, so the density ratio predicted by the ideal-gas adiabat is
(p0​p1​​)1/γ=(1+β)1/γ=1+γβ​−2γ2γ−1​β2+O(β3).(2)
(448)
Equations (1) and (2) agree through order β2. Thus a weak shock satisfies the adiabatic pressure-density relation with an error of order O(β3), which in particular establishes the requested accuracy through O(β2).

For a nonzero real vector x, the Rayleigh quotient of the matrix A is
RA​(x)=xTxxTAx​​.
(449)
The Rayleigh quotient iteration starts from a unit vector v0​. Given vk​, compute the shift
μk​=RA​(vk​),
(450)
solve the linear system
(A−μk​I)wk​=vk​,
(451)
and normalize in the Euclidean norm:
vk+1​=∥wk​∥2​wk​​.
(452)
The next eigenvalue estimate is μk+1​=RA​(vk+1​). The process stops when the eigenpair residual is sufficiently small.

Differentiate the eigenvalue equation
A(t)v(t)=λ(t)v(t)
(453)
at t=0, where A′(0)=E. Suppressing the argument 0 gives
Ev+Av′=λ′v+λv′.
(454)
Left-multiplication by the transpose of the unit left eigenvector u and use of uTA=λuT cancel the terms involving v′:
uTEv=λ′uTv.
(455)
Because the eigenvalue is simple, uTv=0, and hence the first-order perturbation of a simple eigenvalue is
λ′(0)=u(0)Tv(0)u(0)TEv(0)​.
(456)
The definition of the operator norm, followed by the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, gives
∣uTEv∣≤∥u∥2​∥E∥2​∥v∥2​=∥E∥2​.
(457)
Therefore
∣λ′(0)∣≤∣u(0)Tv(0)∣∥E∥2​​​.
(458)

∣uTv∣=1,s(λ)=1​.

More generally, the unitary diagonalization of a normal matrix shows that a real normal matrix also has coincident normalized left and right eigenspaces for each real eigenvalue. Since the question assumes λ∈R, one can again choose u=v, and every such simple eigenvalue has
